interpretation: All 3 records reclassify cleanly from fallback_output to runtime_timeout with the fix in place -- the deadline-swallow fix works exactly as designed: build_completion_forest's TimeoutError now propagates through the compiler-tree loop's check_decode_deadline() instead of being masked as an empty completion forest and certified-fallback'd. This is the 'genuinely out of budget' branch of the finding's own falsification test, not the 'swallow was masking otherwise-fast decode' branch: latency stayed pinned at ~30.0-30.5s (essentially unchanged from the pre-fix total_ms of ~30.0s), so decode is still genuinely blowing the 30s wall on all 3 records -- the fix corrected classification, not speed. A second-order finding: honest classification is strictly worse on meaningful_program_rate for this checkpoint (0.33 pooled before -> 0.0 after), because smoke_callout_01 (offset 2) previously scored meaningful_program_v1=1.0 under the mislabeled fallback_output path -- that 'meaningful' completion was an artifact of the swallowed-timeout certified-fallback content, not a genuine on-time decode. The fix trades an inflated meaningful_program_rate for an honest one; this is the correct trade (I3/decode-invariants: never certify unconstrained-fallback content as ship evidence) but means this checkpoint's true on-time compiler-tree completion rate on this suite is 0/3, not 1/3.
